 2026 NAS Pensacola Homecoming Air Show Takes Flight For Final Day Today
 November 7, 2026
 The 2026 Naval Air Station Pensacola Homecoming Air Show continues today, Saturday, after drawing crowds on opening day Friday.
 General admission to the event is free. The air show serves as one of the area’s largest annual attractions, traditionally drawing more than 250,000 spectators across the weekend.
 For photos from Friday, click here. 
 Themed “200 Years Forged Here,” this year’s air show honors the installation’s bicentennial. Originally established as Naval Shipyard Pensacola in 1826 before transitioning to NAS Pensacola in 1914, the event celebrates two centuries of military presence in Northwest Florida alongside the local community.
 Gates, Schedule, and Entry Requirements 
 Both the Main Gate at the south end of Navy Boulevard and the West Gate at the south end of Blue Angel Parkway open at 8:00 a.m. today. Air show performances are scheduled to begin at 9:30 a.m.
 Installation officials remind attendees that strict identification protocols are enforced at entry checkpoints:
 Everyone over the age of 18 is required to present a REAL ID-compliant state-issued form of identification.
 Foreign nationals must have a valid passport.
 Visitors must observe all local traffic regulations. Parking along the sides of roads entering the installation is strictly prohibited.
 Permitted and Prohibited Items 
 To ensure spectator safety and streamline security screening, base officials have outlined specific guidelines regarding what may and may not be brought onto the airfield.
 Allowed items:
 Small purses
 Diaper bags
 Small camera bags
 Walking sticks for handicap use only
 Service animals
 Prohibited items:
 All weapons (regardless of permit), including firearms, knives (including pocketknives and multi-tools), replica or toy weapons, pepper spray, and stun guns
 Walking sticks (except for handicap assistance)
 Backpacks and large bags
 Coolers and ice chests
 Outside food or beverages
 Pets (service animals permitted)
 Drones
 Bicycles, roller skates, rollerblades, skateboards, and scooters (both kick and electric)
